title: Rebuild-and-diff facts.jsonl in CI
description: CI runs 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)' and byte-compares the result against the committed facts.jsonl. Without this, a hand-edited facts.jsonl passes CI and the deployed site is built from different numbers than the audit trail -- the one thing a provenance gate must prevent. Pure Go, so it costs nothing and preserves the no-LFS-in-CI property.

title: Structural checks: drift, cell relocation, dropped column
description:
- artifact drift: any data/extracted file whose sha256 differs from its manifest entry; any manifest whose source_sha256 differs from the registry; any manifest whose xberg_version differs from the pin
- registry drift (--full only): recomputed PDF sha256 vs sources.yaml
- CELL RELOCATION: independently re-resolve each fact by row_path + column_path and assert the resolved position equals the recorded one. This REPLACES a check that was tautological in an earlier draft -- hashing content and then asserting the content matched can never fail independently. A mismatch means the table shifted, which is precisely the event nothing else detects.
- dropped-column detection: if a page's text has a longer numeric run on a mapped row's label line than the table has columns, fail with 'possible dropped column' (ACFR p34 loses a column silently)

Default verify needs NO PDFs and NO Python; --full adds registry drift and runs monthly with lfs: true.

title: Tier 4: coverage ratchet per (fiscal_year, basis, scope)
description:
A committed coverage_floor; verify fails if measured coverage drops below it. THIS IS WHAT LETS THE GATE LAND BEFORE MAPPING FINISHES: green at 10% coverage, regressions still blocked, floor raised as E7 progresses. Without it, 'department sums match fund totals' would be red throughout the longest epic, and a permanently red gate gets commented out.

Same treatment for transfers: a transfer-unmatched residual node under a coverage floor, since budgets often state aggregate transfers-in without matching per-fund transfers-out.

title: Tier 2: reconciliation with document-derived tolerance
description:
A single exact gate can NEVER go green: the ACFR's MD&A is captioned '(in Millions)' and footnoted 'Due to rounding amounts may differ'. So any comparison against a number PRINTED in the document takes its tolerance from that source's declared precision: 0.5 x unit x n_terms, or ceil(n_terms/2) cents for dollar-precision tables. Rules carry units: dollars|thousands|millions.

Checks: mapped rows sum to the table's stated total row; the computed fund-balance residual equals the document's STATED change in fund balance (this is what turns a tautology into a real cross-check); sum(external expenditure links) equals the published all-funds expenditure total from p66-67.

title: Tier 1: exact, zero-tolerance checks
description: Internal to our own pipeline, so exactness is legitimate: every transfer_id has two equal legs; the graph is acyclic; every link's value_cents equals the sum of its fact_ids; every fund/department/category resolves in funds.yaml/taxonomy.yaml; facts.jsonl is sorted; no ID collisions; AGGREGATION INVARIANCE (the total at every tier depth equals the total at every other depth, which catches double-parented and orphaned nodes); and every derived:true node has a rationale and source_note.

title: E5 Verification
description: Four tiers plus structural checks. Ends with the gate live in CI at a low coverage floor.

title: Map the p66-67 spine only: all-funds control totals
description:
PROVEN IN THE M0 SPIKE: 136 facts map cleanly from these two pages and all 16 column totals tie EXACTLY to the document's own printed totals (General Fund FY2025-26 expenditures $144,650,802; all-funds FY2025-26 revenues $299,969,007).

Structure: rows are 'label followed by N numbers'. p66 carries the labels and the General Fund + Enterprise columns (4 values per row). p67 carries Capital, Debt Service, Special Revenue and Internal Service (8 values per row) with NO labels -- identity is positional from p66 -- and OMITS the all-zero 'Licenses & Permits' row, which must be declared explicitly.

Build the Sankey skeleton from the spine FIRST so the balance checks exist before the detail does. A working reference implementation is in the session scratchpad (spine.py).

title: fisc build emitting facts.jsonl
description: Options struct + NewCmdBuild(f, runF) + private buildRun per byob-command-shape.1; Options.Validate() first, failing with FlagErrorf before any side effects (byob-input-validation.5).

title: Fact model: content-addressed IDs, specified total order
description:
ID = fisc-f-<12 hex of sha256(doc_id|rule_id|row_path|column_path|fiscal_year|basis)>, deliberately EXCLUDING amount_cents and any row/col index -- so a corrected amount is a modified line rather than delete+add, and an upstream row insertion does not renumber the file. An ID collision is a hard build error: two rules claiming the same cell is a real bug.

facts.jsonl total order: (doc_id, page, row_path, column_path, rule_id). Struct-based emission with fixed key order, no omitempty, LF, trailing newline, .gitattributes text eol=lf. verify checks the file is sorted, which catches nondeterminism in CI for free.

title: Locator resolution + ambiguity errors listing candidates
description:
Locator = identity, content-INDEPENDENT. For text: {page, section, row_label, ordinal}. For tables: {page, ordinal_on_page, label_fingerprint, bbox_centroid} where label_fingerprint hashes only non-numeric tokens (strip [0-9,.$()%-]) and the centroid rounds to ~10pt.

Why this is separate from the integrity hash: 16 ACFR tables are byte-identical duplicates of another (one 12-way group across pp.12-23; the Budget Book has a 20-way group), so a content hash is NOT an identity. Resolution must require a unique best match; ambiguity or no-match is a hard error printing the top three candidates with their pages and first rows, via ErrHint (byob-errors.2).

title: Rule schema + parser (substrate: text|table|manual)
description:
Page text is the PRIMARY substrate: tables miss 46% of the Budget Book's money pages, including the spine (p66-67), the transfer schedule (p76), and revenue-by-fund (p127-140). Typed string enums, not iota, for anything crossing YAML/JSON (byob-typed-string-enums-sql).

M0 spike findings that the schema MUST accommodate:
 - a logical table can span pages, and the continuation page may carry NO row labels at all (p67 is a positional continuation of p66)
 - the continuation page OMITS rows that are all-zero across its columns, so a naive positional zip silently shifts every label after the gap. Rules need an explicit omitted_rows declaration plus a row-count assertion that fails loudly on mismatch.
 - column identity is (fund_group, fiscal_year), addressed by a column_path, not by a single header string (headers span two rows and Table.columns is always empty)

title: E4 Mapping engine
description: The core. Ends with facts.jsonl generated from the p66-67 spine.

title: tools/extract.py with a deterministic serializer
description:
Standalone Python run via 'make extract' -- Go NEVER shells out to it, so there is no embedded script and no exception to the pure-Go rule (byob-release.8).

Config verified to work offline with no model download:
  {use_cache: False, disable_ocr: True, output_format: 'markdown',
   pages: {extract_pages: True}, pdf_options: {extract_tables: True, extract_metadata: True}}

Determinism requirements (these are what make committed artifacts stable):
 - sort tables by (page_number, y0, x0); do NOT trust doc.tables order (ACFR p34 emits one logical table as three fragments in REVERSE document order)
 - format floats %.2f; sort_keys=True; fixed indent; ensure_ascii=False; LF; trailing newline
 - record n_cols per table and the page-text line each row came from
 - do NOT treat processing_warnings as a quality signal: it was empty on both documents despite a silently dropped column

Emit pages/pNNNN.md (the PRIMARY substrate) and tables/pNNNN-tNN.json.

title: E2 Extraction
description: tools/extract.py and committed artifacts for all three documents.

title: data/sources.yaml with real URLs, retrieval dates, sha256
description: Doc IDs are already fixed by the committed filenames: livermore-budget-fy2026-2027, livermore-cip-fy2026-2030, livermore-acfr-fy2025. Fields: id, title, publisher, fiscal_years, basis, url, retrieved, file, sha256, pages. The URLs still need to be found on livermoreca.gov. Use the solvent-streets '#@cite' comment convention above hand-entered values. schema_version: 1.

title: internal/amount: strict fail-closed grammar + case table
description:
The most bug-prone code in the project; lands BEFORE any mapping rule exists.

Observed corruption modes that must be REJECTED or handled explicitly:
 1. digits split by whitespace: '2 40,000' for 240,000 (CIP p40) -- REJECT
 2. em-dash-as-zero glued to the next column: ACFR p54 '48,030,349 | -1,315,352 | 49,345,701' where the true reading is +1,315,352 -- REJECT a leading '-' not preceded by a column boundary
 3. '$' bleeding one cell right: p68 ['Wastewater $ ', '27,799,694 $ ', ...] -- strip orphaned $
 4. parenthesis negatives: '(71.8)' -- negative
 5. '-' means zero; '' means ABSENT -- different meanings, both occur, must not be conflated
 6. units vary (dollars/thousands/millions) and come from the rule, not the token
 7. NEW from the M0 spike: '\\-' (backslash-escaped dash) appears in the extracted markdown as a distinct zero token

Amounts are integer cents, never float. Table-driven tests with google/go-cmp per byob-testing.2, in the same commit per byob-testing.4.

title: Import byob decisions into beads
description:
BLOCKED IN THE ORIGINAL SESSION: the sandbox proxy returns 403 on the CONNECT tunnel for GitHub release assets, so the download could not run. Retry from a network that allows it:

  curl -L -o /tmp/byob-decisions.jsonl https://github.com/jcrussell/byob-go-cli/releases/latest/download/issues.jsonl
  bd import /tmp/byob-decisions.jsonl && bd prime

Note bd 1.0.4 warns that 'types.custom' is not a recognized config key but sets it anyway; if 'bd import' rejects the byob records, that warning is the reason to investigate first. Never claim or close a byob-* bead.

title: Go skeleton: cmd/fisc, internal/fisccmd, pkg/cmdutil, pkg/iostreams
description: Three-tier layout per byob-layout.1. main.go is ~20 lines: build Factory, call runner, os.Exit. internal/fisccmd/cmd.go holds Run(root, args, ios) int and the error-to-exit-code mapping per byob-errors.1 (FlagError->2, ErrSilent->1, ErrCancel->2, ExitCodeError->its code, default->1 with 'error: ' on ErrOut). One Factory built in main and threaded into every NewCmdXxx per byob-factory-di.1; expensive deps as lazy closures so --help touches no filesystem. SilenceUsage+SilenceErrors on root per byob-errors.4.

title: E1 Foundations
description: Repo skeleton, CI, and the amount grammar. Ends with green CI on an empty tool.

title: Provenance browser + CSV export
description: Every fact with its source link, and a downloadable CSV. This is the project's real differentiator over the city's own OpenGov page, and it is nearly free once the fact store exists. The provenance panel must resolve by LOCATOR, not fact ID, so a regenerated fact set does not 404 old links.

title: Ten-year trends from the ACFR Statistical Section
description: The richest and cleanest dataset in the corpus, and it needs no joint-distribution inference. ACFR pp.162-195, ~25 ten-year tables: fund balances p163-171, assessed value p173, demographics p180, principal employers p182, FTEs by function, capital assets p184, operating indicators p185, redevelopment debt coverage p194. Verified present by probe.

title: Hand-transcribe the p76 transfer schedule (substrate: manual)
description:
The only published (from-fund, to-fund, amount) table, and it is UNEXTRACTABLE: it comes out as four disjoint text blocks with mismatched cardinalities (21 source labels on one line; destinations split 18/1/3; amounts across three lines interleaved with footnote markers) and zero table objects. Reconstruction requires reading it visually.

21 transfers x 2 years, an afternoon. Guarded by checksum assertions: the hand-entered legs must sum to the page's own stated totals ($21,525,997 FY26, $21,624,633 FY27) AND to the TRANSFER IN row of the citywide schedule. That is a stronger provenance story than a fragile auto-parse.

title: GF revenue by source (p127-140)
description: Revenue Sources by Fund, line-item. Each row carries FOUR columns -- FY23-24 actual, FY24-25 revised, FY25-26 budget, FY26-27 budget -- so this also produces the trend series in E8 with no extra extraction. Watch the contra-revenue rows (ERAF, RPTTF) on p127.

title: GF department x object category (p167)
description: 'General Fund Expenditures by Major Category'. This is the ONLY place the department-by-category JOINT distribution is published -- elsewhere the city publishes 'Expenditures by Category' (by division) and 'Department Funding Sources' (by fund) as two marginals of the same total, never the joint. Public Works p124-125 has 5 divisions x 5 categories on one side and 22 funds on the other, both summing to $78,707,657, with nothing tying them. So tier 5 exists ONLY inside the General Fund; anywhere else it would require inventing numbers.

title: E7 Coverage
description: The bulk of the labour. Each task raises the coverage floor.

title: pages.yml deploy
description:
On push to main: checkout WITHOUT LFS (the site does not need the PDFs), fisc build, fisc export -o dist --clean, upload-pages-artifact, deploy-pages. Actions pinned by SHA.

Keeping LFS out of CI matters: GitHub's free tier is 1GB/month bandwidth and each LFS checkout is ~70MB, so ~14 checkouts exhaust it. Consequence for the frontend: raw.githubusercontent.com serves LFS POINTER TEXT, not the PDF, so the site must link to the city's canonical URL with #page=N plus the committed pages/pNNNN.md on github.com.

title: fisc export with output-path safety
description: Resolve and containment-check the output dir before the work starts (byob-input-validation.1). Copy solvent-streets' SafeCleanDir: refuse to delete a non-empty directory that lacks an index.html sentinel, so a mistyped --output cannot wipe user data. Share the template parse path with any future serve command so the two cannot drift.

title: internal/export: templates, app.js, vendored d3-sankey
description:
LOAD THE dataviz SKILL FIRST for palette, the constraint-tier treatment (it must not compete with fund identity for hue), and legend/tooltip rules.

Go html/template owns the page and injects window.FISC_CONFIG for metadata; the browser fetches data/*.json for bulk. app.js is plain browser JS with JSDoc types checked by tsc --checkJs -- NOT TypeScript sources, NOT a bundler; npm never appears in the deploy path. This matches solvent-streets, which uses npm for lint only. d3 and d3-sankey are VENDORED into site/vendor so the published site has no third-party runtime dependency. All asset paths relative, plus a zero-byte .nojekyll -- that combination removes base-path configuration entirely.

title: internal/project: projection interface + sankey
description:
One file per projection behind a common interface (byob-interfaces.1), with site/data holding one JSON per projection. PUT THE SEAM IN NOW, while there is exactly one projection -- retrofitting after three exist is the expensive version.

Sankey specifics: link.kind in {external, internal_transfer, internal_service}; the headline total sums ONLY external links, because naively summing the expenditure column gives $313,708,146 when the city spends $254,095,412 (a 23% inflation from transfers counted twice). Transfers are paired transfer-out/transfer-in synthetic nodes sharing a transfer_id, which keeps the graph acyclic. Explicit fund-balance-draw / fund-balance-contribution nodes rather than silent padding. Contra-revenue (ERAF -$15,857,875, RPTTF -$1,891,804 in FY26, ~26% of gross property tax) nets into its parent with sign: contra -- a Sankey cannot render a negative link.

title: Node tier hierarchy + constraint_tier; client-side aggregation
description:
Six tiers: 0 revenue source, 1 constraint tier, 2 fund group (the six columns of the p66-67 spine), 3 fund, 4 department, 5 object category. Emit FINEST-GRAIN LINKS ONLY plus node.parent/node.tier; the client aggregates to the selected depth and unions child fact_ids for the provenance panel.

Default General Fund view renders tiers 0,3,4 (+5 on drill-down); the All City Funds toggle renders 0,1,2,3. Tier 1 is the mandatory-vs-discretionary analogue and is mostly PUBLISHED, so it can be cited rather than invented -- but any editorial classification (e.g. calling Wages & Benefits MOU-fixed) must be marked derived:true with a rationale.

title: E6 First site
description: Ends with a live, ugly, correct Pages deploy showing the spine control totals.

title: Automate the four break-it scenarios as CI tests
description:
These are the acceptance test for the provenance claim, and they target the failure modes that actually matter rather than the ones that are easy to trigger:
 1. insert a row above a mapped row -> output must be 'row moved, re-anchor', not a silent wrong-cell read
 2. bump the pinned xberg and re-extract -> failure must be a reviewable diff plus a working 'fisc reanchor --accept', not N dead anchors
 3. change one number so the cell text still parses -> tier 2 arithmetic must catch it
 4. hand-edit facts.jsonl -> rebuild-and-diff must reject it
Assert on behavior, not call counts (byob-testing.3).

title: Tier 3: reconciliations.yaml, declared exceptions with expiry
description: Each entry {check_id, expected_delta_cents, reason, source_quote, reviewed, expires}. verify fails if the observed delta differs from the declared delta (drift still caught), fails on an EXPIRED entry, and fails on an UNUSED entry (dead exceptions rot). You can pin a discrepancy with a written reason; you cannot silence one.

title: Integrity hash check as a distinct error class, with a diff
description: expected_content_hash is checked AFTER the locator resolves. A mismatch is a DIFFERENT error from 'not found': 'located at page N, content changed' plus a unified diff of stored vs current normalized rows. Normalize hard before hashing (collapse whitespace, NBSP, soft hyphen, unicode minus, $, parenthesis negatives, trailing empty columns) and record normalizer_version so 'xberg changed' stays distinguishable from 'our normalizer changed'.

title: data/taxonomy.yaml controlled vocabulary
description: Prevents 'taxes/property' here and 'tax/property' there. Also declares every DERIVED classification with a rationale and a source_note -- the 'published vs derived' rule is enforced against this file. Facts are numbers the city printed; classifications may be our judgment, and the UI must mark the difference.

title: E3 Registries
description: Canonical fund registry and controlled vocabulary. Pure data entry; parallelizable with E4.

title: data/funds.yaml from Budget Book p253-254
description:
One-time transcription of the 'List of Funds by Fund Type' appendix, keyed on the city's own stable numeric fund IDs. Fields: number, name, type, gasb_category, constraint_tier, restriction_note, major.

constraint_tier is one of restricted-by-law | committed | discretionary and drives the tier-1 Sankey nodes. Cited sources: fund types p253-254 and 'Description of Funds' p258; GASB 54 reserve classes (nonspendable/restricted/committed/assigned/unassigned) at ACFR p52, notes p92-94, ten-year at ACFR p167.

This is the reconciliation layer between the Budget Book's ~110 named funds and the ACFR's three-column presentation.

title: Extract all three docs; commit artifacts; copy testdata fixtures
description: Whole corpus extracts in ~10s total (measured). Commit data/extracted/** (NOT via LFS -- text should diff). Copy a handful of real page markdown and table JSON into testdata/ so Go tests never need Python, the PDFs, or the network.

title: Manifest writer: atomic, versioned, hashed
description: Per byob-storage.8 and byob-runtime-directories.3/.4. Records xberg_version, extraction config hash, normalizer_version, source_sha256 (must match the registry), page_count, table_count, warnings, and a sha256 for every emitted artifact. Atomic write = temp file in the SAME directory, Sync, Rename. schema_version in the file.

title: Pin xberg exactly in requirements.txt
description: Currently xberg 1.0.14 in /home/ubuntu/venv. Pin the exact version; verify will fail when a manifest's xberg_version differs from the pin (byob-security.1). Without the pin the manifest's xberg_version field is decoration.

title: Makefile, .golangci.yml, .golangci-version, AGENTS.md
description: Makefile is the day-to-day entrypoint per byob-release.3: build install test lint fmt vet extract clean. -trimpath always; -s -w on release only (byob-release.6). Pin the lint floor in a one-line .golangci-version read by both CI and the Makefile. AGENTS.md is ours -- do NOT copy byob's CLAUDE.md or README.md into this repo; point at 'bd prime'. Note bd init already wrote a CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json here.

title: ci.yml: lint, format, build, test -race, vet, govulncheck, mod-tidy
description: Model on solvent-streets .github/workflows/ci.yaml: parallel jobs, all actions pinned by commit SHA with a version comment, permissions: contents: read (byob-security.5). No LFS in this workflow -- see the LFS bandwidth note in the plan. The verify job is added in E5.

title: Staffing / FTE
description: Authorized positions, Budget Book p247-252 ('Regular, At-Will or Limited Duration'). Pairs with the ACFR's ten-year FTE-by-function table.

title: CIP project explorer
description: Filter/search projects by program, fund and year. CIP p40-41 program summaries and per-project funding tables are the one place table extraction works WELL (52% recall overall but these pages extract cleanly). Same two filters as the CIP node work: appropriated years only, new appropriations only.

title: Line-item revenue trends
description: Every revenue row on p127-140 already carries four fiscal-year columns (FY23-24 actual, FY24-25 revised, FY25-26 and FY26-27 budget), so each line is a 4-point series with NO extra extraction once E7's GF revenue mapping exists.

title: Fund explorer
description: Sources/uses and reserves per fund with the restricted flag made explicit -- the thing the Sankey can only gesture at. Source: Fund Balances by Major/Non-Major Fund, Budget Book p68-75, plus funds.yaml.

title: Department pages
description: The view most residents actually want: what does Police cost and who pays for it. Source: the per-department pages (Expenditures by Category by division, Department Funding Sources by fund) plus performance measures (e.g. p48).

title: E8 Further projections
description: The fact store is the product; the Sankey is one projection. Each of these is independent -- pick by interest.

title: CIP funds as nodes: appropriated years, new appropriations only
description:
The CIP is NOT double-counted inside the operating budget -- verified arithmetically to the dollar:
  transfers OUT (p66-67)          59,612,734
  transfers IN  (p66-67)        - 21,525,997
  gap to CIP funds                38,086,737
  + CIP grants direct (p222)    +  8,997,886
                                  47,084,623  == stated FY2025-26 CIP appropriation (p222)

So the citywide schedule already contains the CIP as a $38.1M transfer-out that goes NOWHERE unless CIP funds are modelled as nodes. The diagram does not balance without them. Bridge table is p222 ('CIP Project Fund (Receiving) / Operating Fund (Transferring)'); dedicated CIP funds are listed at p253-254.

TWO HARD FILTERS: only FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 are appropriated (the CIP's tables run to FY2030-45, which is planning intent, not budget); and the CIP's $141.3M two-year figure includes $35.2M of carry-forward (p211), so only the $106.1M of NEW appropriations is FY26+FY27 money.

title: ACFR as a separate function-axis view (scope: governmental-net)
description:
NOT a sibling in a year toggle -- it is structurally a different chart. The ACFR has three fund columns (General, Low Income Housing, Other Governmental), an expenditure axis by FUNCTION (Police, Fire, Public Works) rather than object category, ISF eliminated, and $55,286,695 of fiduciary custodial payments that are not the city's money (declare fiduciary out of scope with a note on the page). There is no object-category breakdown anywhere in the ACFR.

The UI must never offer a year-toggle between datasets of different scope. Label it as a different accounting basis.

title: All-funds toggle rendering tiers 0-3 with the constraint tier
description:
The General Fund is $144.7M of $254.1M (57%); the other 43% is water/sewer/airport ratepayer money, gas tax, impact fees, assessments and grants, almost all legally restricted. A single all-funds Sankey makes the visual claim that money pools and is then allocated, which is false for that 43% -- water rates cannot pay for police. So all-funds is a deliberate second click, and restricted funds render as a visually separated, labelled band driven by funds.yaml constraint_tier, not merely a different hue.

Also surface the Internal Service Fund double-count: ISF expenditures are $25,077,367 whose $18,969,834 of revenue is charges to other city departments, already counted inside those departments. The ACFR eliminates ISF activity; the Budget Book does not.

title: fisc reanchor --accept
description: Bulk-rewrites integrity hashes after a reviewed extraction change. This is what converts an xberg bump from 're-anchor N rules blind' into one commit with a readable diff.

title: Schema-validation test over every committed data file
description: Every file under data/ validates against its schema_version. Runs in CI over the whole tree.

title: Determinism test: re-extract a fixture, assert byte-identical
description: Determinism is already confirmed empirically (ACFR run 3x, identical hashes); this test keeps it true. Note doc.tables order was stable across three single-machine runs but is not documented as stable across core counts -- the explicit sort in the serializer is what removes that dependency.

title: Gann appropriations limit
description: Budget Book p38, 'Constitutional Spending Limits'. Small, and genuinely interesting: the limit vs actual appropriations.
